newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond trade ideas - Into U.S. out of Can dollars.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond trade ideas - Into U.S. out of Can dollars.

text.p: Bond analysts' latest Eurobond trade ideas featured Eurolire, Eurodollars and a cross-market Eurodollar-Euro-Canadian dollar switch.
San Paolo have a bearish outlook on the Eurolire market as they expect a series of Bank of Italy rate cuts throughout 1997 which will flatten the yield curve in the medium term.
Sanwa International recommends buying a 6.0 percent Bayerische Vereinsbank U.S. dollar bond due December 1999 and selling a 7.25 percent Norway Canadian dollar bond due October 1998.

Sanwa said that there are favourable cross-over rates between the two markets, with a low of -24 basis points in the last six months to a current level of +145.5 b.p. Contributing to this is the Bank of Canada's easier monetary policy to stem the Canadian dollar's appreciation against the U.S. dollar. Once stabilised, however, the central bank is expected to stop cutting interest rates.
Sanwa also advises that outright short positions in Euro-Canadian dollar bonds should be avoided because of the expensive borrowing costs of these securities.
**Following are latest trade ideas, compiled by Reuters**
STRATEGY Helaba is cheap against the swap and BTP at 17 b.p. and 7 b.p. respectively. This credit neutral switch also offers around a 12 b.p. pick-up in yield.
STRATEGY Bank Austria is cheap against the swap at 18 b.p. through compared to BayerLB which is at 27 b.p. through. Bank Austria also offers around a 10 b.p. pick-up for the same duration.
STRATAGY SEK is cheap against the swap and BTP trading at 9 b.p. and 15 b.p. through respectively. This move also offers near a 15 b.p. pick-up in yield.
STRATEGY EIB offers around a 12 b.p. pick-up in yield and is cheap against the swap at 23 b.p. through and BTP at 26 b.p. through.
STRATEGY The 10.75 percent bond is cheaper against the swap and BTP and offers around a 13 b.p. pick-up in yield for shorter duration.

STRATEGY This switch offers a yield pick-up 171 b.p. The BayerVB bond is a relatively new issue so lacks a yield history, yet the performance between three-year eurodollar and euro-Canadian swap rates shows that in the last six months (out of Canadian dollars into U.S. dollars) the differential has widened from a low of -24 b.p. to a current level of +145.5 b.p.
One reason for this differential is the Bank of Canada's easing of monetary policy to counter the Canadian dollar's appreciation.
